llm.summary: The skill has a legitimate delegation purpose, but it needs review because it runs unattended CodeBuddy jobs with auto-approval while loading repository project settings that may execute hooks.

dimensions.detail: The clean-environment wrapper is purpose-aligned, but it unconditionally adds `--setting-sources project`, so repository-controlled CodeBuddy settings can affect an unattended permission-bypassed run in the target workspace.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package contains a Markdown skill and a JavaScript launcher. I found no hidden installer, remote payload fetch, or automatic dependency installation; the launcher locates an existing CodeBuddy CLI and spawns it.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses many controls, including human authorization for dangerous operations, but it also uses broad activation phrases and treats `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` as required for write runs without requiring review of project-level settings or hooks first.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill openly writes prompts and logs under `.cli-runs/` and references CodeBuddy session logs under `~/.codebuddy/projects/`; this supports auditability but can retain sensitive prompts, paths, code context, or accidental secrets unless users manage retention and version-control exclusions.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The purpose is coherent: delegate large CodeBuddy CLI coding or audit jobs, manage budgets, logs, models, and independent verification. The capability is high-impact because it explicitly supports unattended file editing, Bash-capable subagents, and permission bypass for write batches.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intentionally want CodeBuddy to run unattended coding batches. Use it in repositories you trust or in a sandboxed/containerized copy, inspect project-level CodeBuddy settings and hooks before using auto-approval, keep secrets out of prompts, and exclude `.cli-runs/` plus CodeBuddy session logs from commits and backups when they may contain sensitive data.
llm.findings:
[T09] unexpected: Accepted as a material review concern. The launcher always passes `--setting-sources project`, and the documented workflow uses `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`; the artifact does not require inspecting or disabling repository project hooks before unattended runs.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Partly accepted. Broad trigger phrases are not malicious by themselves, but they can unintentionally activate a high-impact unattended delegation workflow.
[RA2] expected: Accepted as disclosed but still relevant. Persistent local logs and session files are expected for audit, yet users should treat them as potentially sensitive and exclude or delete them as appropriate.
[LP3] unexpected: Downgraded. The frontmatter does not declare allowed tools, but the artifact explains its CLI, file, logging, and execution behavior in detail; the main concern is scoping of high-impact execution, not opacity of purpose.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded. The skill is mainly written in Chinese, but I did not find instructions forcing the agent to ignore a user's chosen language or locale.
[RP1] expected: Downgraded. The referenced `npx jest` example is a test-running example, not installation of an MCP server or core runtime dependency.
